findings.title: immediateDelete path keeps the old failure mode and leaves the reminder row behind
findings.body:
When `immediateDelete` is true (used by the reschedule path in `handleNewBooking.ts:968`, the workflow-delete path and the deleted-step path in `workflows.tsx:214/521`) the function still performs a synchronous `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends { status: "cancel" }` and then returns.

Two problems:
1. This is exactly the call the PR description identifies as unreliable (SendGrid keeps cancelled batches in `scheduled_sends` and caps pending cancellations at 100). Any failure is swallowed by the surrounding `catch` that only `console.log`s, and because the row is neither marked `cancelled` nor deleted, the new CRON-based retry mechanism will never pick it up. The reminder email for the rescheduled booking is therefore still sent – the exact bug this PR claims to fix for rescheduled bookings.
2. Unlike the `!referenceId` branch (which deletes the row) and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (which deletes the row), this branch leaves the `WorkflowReminder` row in the DB pointing at the old/cancelled booking until the cron's `deleteMany` eventually removes it when `scheduledDate` has passed.

For reschedules it would be safer to use the same deferred mechanism (set `cancelled: true`) instead of the one-shot immediate cancel.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget and may never be committed
findings.body:
The previous code pushed `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany(...)` into `prismaPromises` and awaited them before returning. Now `deleteScheduledEmailReminder()` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder()` are async functions invoked inside `forEach` without `await` and their promises are never collected, so the handler can return its 200 response while the `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ data: { cancelled: true } })` (or the Twilio cancel + row delete) is still in flight. In a serverless deployment the function can be frozen/terminated right after the response, so the `cancelled` flag is never persisted and the reminder email is still delivered for the cancelled booking. Errors are also swallowed inside the helpers, so this fails silently.

The same pattern was introduced at `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488` (where `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` was removed) and `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966`. These calls should be collected and awaited.

findings.title: One failing SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation batch and skips all DB deletes
findings.body: The `for` loop over `remindersToCancel` is wrapped in a single `try/catch`. If `client.request` throws for one reminder (invalid/expired batch id, rate limit, SendGrid 4xx/5xx), the loop is abandoned: every remaining reminder in this run is not cancelled, and – because `prisma.workflowReminder.delete()` returns a lazy `PrismaPromise` that is only executed when awaited at line 74 – none of the already-cancelled reminders are deleted either. A single permanently failing `referenceId` therefore blocks cancellation of every other reminder on every subsequent cron run, which reproduces the "reminders still sent" bug this PR fixes. Each iteration should have its own try/catch (and the delete should be awaited per reminder). The query also has no `take` limit, so a large backlog can exceed the function timeout.

findings.title: Deferred cancellation can miss SendGrid's cancellation deadline for imminent reminders
findings.body: Cancelling/rescheduling now never cancels the SendGrid send immediately; it only sets `cancelled: true` and relies on the `scheduleEmailReminders` cron (runs every 15 min, cancels reminders whose `scheduledDate` is within the next hour). SendGrid only honours a cancellation submitted sufficiently far ahead of the scheduled send (documented as at least 10 minutes). If a booking is cancelled, say, 12 minutes before the reminder's `sendAt`, the next cron tick can be up to 15 minutes later – i.e. after the send time – so the reminder email is still delivered for a cancelled/rescheduled booking. Consider cancelling immediately (and still marking `cancelled: true` so the cron can retry) when `scheduledDate` is close to now.

findings.title: Cancellation query is not restricted to scheduled SendGrid email reminders
findings.body: `remindersToCancel` selects every `WorkflowReminder` with `cancelled: true`, without filtering `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` or `referenceId: { not: null }`. The `cancelled` column is on the shared model, so any SMS row (or a row with a null `referenceId`) that ever gets `cancelled: true` would be sent to SendGrid as `batch_id: <twilio sid|null>`; the request fails and, per the single shared try/catch around the loop, aborts all remaining cancellations. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` and `referenceId: { not: null }` to the where clause.

findings.title: Unused `Prisma` import and type-only identifiers moved into a value import
findings.body: `Prisma` is added to the `@prisma/client` value import but is no longer used anywhere in the file (the only remaining use, `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>[]`, was deleted in this diff), which will fail `no-unused-vars` in CI. The same import also converts the previous `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` into a value import of type-only identifiers (also done in `handleNewBooking.ts:1-10` for `App`, `Credential`, `EventTypeCustomInput`, `Prisma`), which conflicts with the `import type` convention used throughout the repo/`consistent-type-imports`. Additionally the new member is added without a trailing comma (`Prisma\n} from "@prisma/client";`), so the prettier check will fail. The unrelated re-indentation of the large commented-out `testAction` block (lines ~901-1009) suggests this file was taken from an older branch; please rebase.

findings.title: New `cancelled` flag is nullable with no index backing the cron query
findings.body: `cancelled Boolean?` (and the migration `ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN`) has no default, so every existing and newly created row stores NULL and all call sites must use `cancelled: true` rather than a boolean comparison (easy to get wrong later – `@default(false)` would be safer). More importantly, `WorkflowReminder` has no index on `cancelled`/`scheduledDate`, yet the new cron query `findMany({ where: { cancelled: true, scheduledDate: { lte: ... } } })` – plus the existing `deleteMany` and unscheduled-reminder scan – runs every 15 minutes over a table that grows with every booking, resulting in repeated full table scans.
